table_title: List the United States presidents who held office for any portion of the 20th century (1 January 1901 to 31 December 2000), with the year their term began, the year their term ended, their political party, and the names of all individuals who served as their Vice President.
db_analog: SELECT president, term_start_year, term_end_year, party, vice_presidents FROM us_presidents WHERE term_overlaps_period('1901-01-01', '2000-12-31') ORDER BY president
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of presidents of the United States' master article, accessed 2026-05-11. Universe is the 18 US presidents who held office for any portion of the 20th century (defined as 1 January 1901 through 31 December 2000 inclusive), as listed in the master wikitable; the filter includes McKinley (term March 1897 to September 1901, served Jan-Sept 1901 of the 20th century) and Clinton (term January 1993 to January 2001, served all of 1993-2000 plus 20 days of January 2001) and excludes George W. Bush (term started 20 January 2001, after the 20th century ended). Per-row cells are taken verbatim from the master wikitable's rowspan-expanded structure: the Name column supplies the staged President name with the disambiguating birth-death year markers stripped; the Term column supplies the Term Start Year (year of inauguration) and Term End Year (year of leaving office, regardless of cause); the Party column supplies the Party cell (Republican or Democratic across all 18 rows in this window — no third-party president in the 20th century); the Vice President column supplies the Vice President(s) cell, with the master table's per-term rowspan'd entries deduplicated, sorted alphabetically, semicolon-delimited within a single cell, and with 'Vacant' interval entries filtered out (since vacant periods are not vice-presidential appointments). Three presidents have multi-VP cells: Franklin D. Roosevelt (Garner 1933-1941, Wallace 1941-1945, Truman 1945) per the source's three rowspan'd VP entries during his four-term presidency; Richard Nixon (Agnew 1969-1973, Ford 1973-1974) per the source's two rowspan'd entries reflecting Agnew's October 1973 resignation; William McKinley (Hobart 1897-1899, Theodore Roosevelt 1901) per the source's two rowspan'd entries reflecting Hobart's November 1899 death and Roosevelt's March 1901 swearing-in. The underlying biographical facts (party affiliation, term dates, vice-presidential succession) are stable on a multi-decade horizon and have not changed since the snapshot date.
_extraction_notes: Verbatim seed #18 ('20th-century US presidents × attrs') instance, filling `multi_attribute_projection` gap 2 → gap 1 (saturation: 7 of 8 target). Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, source_count = 1 — the master 'List of presidents of the United States' Wikipedia article is the canonical single source covering all 4 per-row attribute columns. The master table contains 1 wikitable with 84 rows (1 header + 83 data rows covering presidents 1 through 47, of which 18 are in the 20th-century window). Pipeline: (1) fetch the cited Wikipedia article HTML, (2) parse the lone wikitable with rowspan-aware extraction (pandas.read_html with default flavor expands per-term rows for multi-term presidents into separate row entries for each (President, Election) pair, with the Name/Term/Party cells rowspan'd over all sub-rows), (3) filter to No. ∈ [25, 42] (the 20th-century window — president 25 William McKinley through 42 Bill Clinton; president 43 George W. Bush is excluded because his term began January 20, 2001, after the 20th century ended on December 31, 2000), (4) for each president, take Name verbatim (stripping the disambiguating (birth-death) suffix and footnote markers), take Term Start Year and Term End Year as the 4-digit year components of the Term cell's begin and end dates, take Party verbatim (Republican or Democratic — both Whigs and Democratic-Republicans are pre-20th-century parties and don't appear in the 18-row window), and take Vice President(s) as the rowspan-expanded set of VPs deduplicated, alphabetized, and semicolon-delimited within a single cell (Vacant-interval entries like 'Vacant through March 4, 1925' or 'Vacant after November 21, 1899' are filtered out because vacant periods are not vice-presidential appointments). Result: 18 rows × 5 columns, PK on President, 0 duplicates. Party distribution: Republican 11, Democratic 7 (no third-party president in the 20th century, although Theodore Roosevelt later ran on the Bull Moose ticket in 1912 — but his 1901-1909 presidency was Republican). Term-year range: starts span 1897 (McKinley) to 1993 (Clinton); ends span 1901 (McKinley) to 2001 (Clinton). Three multi-VP rows: McKinley (2 VPs across his 1.5 terms), Nixon (2 VPs across his ~5.5 years), Franklin D. Roosevelt (3 VPs across his four terms — the largest VP count in US history). All other 15 rows have exactly 1 VP. Note that McKinley's first term (1897-1901) is partly in the 19th century but his 20th-century portion (January 1, 1901 to September 14, 1901, when he died from gunshot wounds) qualifies him under the 'served any portion of the 20th century' filter; his Term Start Year cell is 1897 (the source's start year, verbatim), not 1901. Similarly Clinton's Term End Year cell is 2001 (verbatim from the source's January 20, 2001 end date), not 2000. Confidence gradient is real: very-LLM-knowable rows include the canonical Cold War / modern presidents (Eisenhower, Kennedy, Johnson, Nixon, Reagan, Clinton) and the major transformative presidents (FDR, Truman); harder calibration cells include the early-20th-century presidents (Harding 1921-1923, Coolidge 1923-1929, Hoover 1929-1933) and their lesser-known VPs (Charles G. Dawes for Coolidge, Charles Curtis for Hoover, Garret Hobart for McKinley); the multi-VP cells (FDR's three VPs, Nixon's two VPs, McKinley's two VPs) test whether the LLM knows the complete VP sequence per president rather than just the most famous VP.
